teaches: How a thing works: open on the one idea that makes it different; the mechanism in order; then what it removes; land on the reason that matters most, not on adoption numbers.

packet.title: How passkeys work
sentences: A passkey replaces a password with a pair of cryptographic keys.
The public key is sent to the website, and the private key stays on the user's device.
The private key is protected by a fingerprint, face scan or screen PIN.
Something signed with the private key can be checked with the public key, but the public key cannot reveal the private one.
At login the website sends a random challenge, which the device signs and sends back.
A passkey is tied to the real website's address, so a lookalike site cannot get a signature.

packet.title: Why passkeys stop phishing
sentences: A breach of a website's database exposes only public keys, which cannot be used to log in.
Most stolen accounts are taken by tricking people into typing their password on a fake page.
Several large technology companies now support passkeys.
